title: The 1925 Victor session and Rappolo walking off
summary: At the Victor session in New Orleans Rappolo and Pecora quarreled and Rappolo walked off, so Cadello switched to clarinet.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I was going to ask about the Victor session, too. Do you remember any details of that?

Yes, I do. That Victor session, Victor people came out here and contacted Paul, and they liked the band. That was the 1925 band. It was here in New Orleans. Well, Paul had a lot of, I don't want to say a lot, but he had bad luck in it. Charlie Cudelo was going to play tenor sax, Santa and trombone, and Red Long and Leo Addy, and that particular day they were going to record, Santo and Rap had a little falling out. So Rap walked off the set, and Paul went through it anyhow, and he made Charlie get off the tenor and go on to clarinet, Charlie Cudelo. That's how that happened. Yeah, and he took the Crying For Me blues solo, but he wouldn't take it like Rap took it, so he changed it around and so forth and so on, but that's what happened on that particular session. They just had to have a little hard feelings that day when they were going to record, and Rap walked off.
